document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban "Threat Warning" (Islama 09424)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret (NODIS)] The Taliban send an unspecific message that terrorists backed by Ahmed Shah Massoud and Iranian intelligence are plotting against the U.S. State believes the motives are probably political, since Massoud and Iran are among the Taliban's most powerful enemies.

persons.name: Ahmad Shah Masood
persons.role: Taliban political and military enemy; anti-Taliban commander accused by Taliban of planning terrorist act

mentions.quote: AGENTS OF AHMAD SHAH MASOOD, THEIR POLITICAL AND MILITARY ENEMY

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Subject of earlier US message to Taliban regarding his activities; made media statements

mentions.quote: THE LAST MESSAGE WE GAVE TO THE TALIBAN REGARDING BIN LADIN'S ACTIVITIES
DISTANCE BETWEEN THEM AND UBL AFTER HIS LATEST STATEMENTS TO THE MEDIA
CHARGE CONVENED AN AD HOC MEETING OF CONCERNED SECTIONS

persons.name: Joe Novak
persons.role: Political officer (POLOFF), US Embassy Islamabad; addressee of Taliban letter under the name 'John Wick'

mentions.quote: FYI JOHN WICK IS UNDOUBTEDLY POLOFF JOE NOVAK.

key_claims: The Taliban-controlled Afghan embassy warned the US of a supposed plot by Masood's men and Iranian intelligence to attack a US embassy in an unspecified country.
US Embassy officials unanimously judged the warning to be a political statement or possible disinformation.
The Taliban may have been motivated by a rumored US–Masood rapprochement.
The letter lacked detailed or verifiable information, paralleling the US message to the Taliban about bin Ladin's activities.
The letter may have been meant to create distance between the Taliban and Usama bin Ladin after his media statements.
